what_it_does: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is an AI architecture where a large model is divided into many specialized sub-networks called 'experts'; for each input, only a small fraction of experts are activated, keeping computation manageable while the total number of parameters (the model's learned knowledge, stored as numbers) stays very large. The problem is that this large parameter count — sometimes hundreds of billions of numbers — far exceeds the fast memory (called VRAM) inside a typical graphics card, so the expert weights must be stored in the computer's main RAM or even on a storage drive and fetched when needed, creating a severe data-movement bottleneck. MoE-Lightning pipelines this process: while the GPU (a chip with thousands of cores for parallel math) is computing with one expert's weights, the system is simultaneously streaming the next expert's weights from CPU memory into the GPU in small pages. A mathematical model that accounts for the GPU's compute speed, the GPU's fast memory size, the CPU's memory size, and the data-transfer rate between them guides the system in choosing the right batch size and pipelining strategy automatically.
